email.subject: Your card was paused after an unusual payment

body.v: We paused a card payment of CHF 389.00 that looked unusual. Your card stays paused until you confirm it.
Please open the SwissAlpBank app within 24 hours and tell us whether the payment was yours.
We will never ask you for a code, a password or your card number by email, text or phone.

hotspots.explain: The address is on swissalpbank.example, the bank's real domain.
A real deadline, but it asks you to use the app you already have. Urgency alone does not make an email a scam.
It says clearly that it will never ask for a code or password.
There is no link. You are sent to the app, a channel you control.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: SwissAlpBank: the address is on swissalpbank.example and nothing points to another domain.

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Some urgency, because a payment was paused and there is a 24-hour window. But the pressure is a real deadline, with no threat.
choices: Some urgency, from a real deadline

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Open the app and say whether the payment was yours. No code, no link, no password.
choices: Reply with the code from your phone
Check a payment in the bank's app

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Open the SwissAlpBank app yourself, or call the number on the back of your card.
choices: Click a link in the email

actions.label: Open the SwissAlpBank app yourself and check the payment
actions.consequence: The payment is listed and you confirm or deny it.

actions.label: Call the number on the back of your card
actions.consequence: The bank confirms the paused payment.

actions.label: Reply with the code if one arrives
actions.consequence: The email said they would never ask. A code must never be given away, even to a real bank.

attacker_reveal: This one is real, dear, even though it has a deadline. The domain is the bank's own, nobody asks for a code and you are sent to the app. Compare it with the 'case 7731' email: both are calm, but only one asks you to read out a code.
